task: T02 / F02 — FDE timestamp contract and separately verified browser-harness correction

environment.ci_parity: Declared Node engine satisfied; Ubuntu / CI Node 22 parity not established.

patches.scope: Strict non-leap-second RFC3339 parsing, four field-specific guards, three real-digest behavioral tests, generated test count and site manifest.
Only the context test server: use native ThreadingHTTPServer; remove unused socketserver import. No product code change.

commands.tooling: Use the bundled Node 24.19.0 runtime and a local Python 3.11.16 venv on PATH; install pinned requirements-dev.txt only in that venv. Reuse the matching Playwright Chromium cache.

checks.name: instrumented original context harness
observed: Imported module connection reset / socket not connected

checks.name: same browser diagnostic with threaded context server only
exact baseline plus harness patch only: context browser check
timestamp plus separate harness correction: full gate
separate and combined exact-base patch applicability; diff whitespace

research.use: Mandatory date/time components, offsets, case variants and fractional seconds.
Gregorian day bounds and leap-second restrictions.
The schema date-time format references RFC3339.
Vendor documents threaded servers for browser preopened sockets that can block a single-thread server.

limitations: The timestamp-only full gate failed. Only the combined timestamp and separately disclosed context-harness correction passed the full gate. This does not mean the timestamp change corrected HTTP transport.

RFC3339 permits announced leap seconds. Native Date cannot parse second 60 in either baseline or candidate. At packet level the baseline rejects the two required-field cases but accepts the two nullable-field cases through the original parsing gap; the candidate rejects all four. Maintainers must document the supported subset or choose a deliberate leap-second policy. This proposal does not claim complete RFC3339 acceptance.
Native Date retains the existing millisecond comparison precision and truncates finer fractions. Sub-millisecond ordering is not newly implemented.
Existing chronology, five-minute future-skew limit, freshness states, integrity logic and legacy 0.2 inspection rules are preserved.

The release browser suite reported its pre-existing sandbox-fallback static routing for seven display modes. The context suite passed over native localhost HTTP after the separate harness correction. No new fallback, retry or product workaround was introduced.
Independent candidate proposals are not upstream implementation or maintainer acceptance. No upstream source repository was modified remotely.
Public synthetic fixtures and local verification only; no private data, authenticated-origin verification, human/device accessibility attestation or hosted release equivalence.

remaining_scope_limits: This closes the local Node22-major compatibility gap only. macOS arm64 is not the declared ubuntu-latest runner or a hosted GitHub Actions execution.
The workflow uses Node major 22; the exact hosted minor, npm and runner Python versions were not queried or reproduced. This run records official Node22.23.3/npm10.9.9/Python3.11.16 explicitly.
The timestamp-only full gate still fails. Only the independently corrected harness and combined configuration pass their applicable browser gates. Timestamp validation did not fix transport.
The earlier Node24 results and failure diagnostics remain historical evidence; this supplement adds observations rather than overwriting them.

The seven release-browser display modes retain the existing reported sandbox-fallback static route. The harness-only and combined context checks use native localhost HTTP. No new fallback, retry or validation weakening was introduced.
No leap-second policy or sub-millisecond precision change was introduced. Existing owner-dependent contract decisions remain open.
Hosted CodeQL Actions initialization/analysis, Ubuntu OS dependency installation, release packaging/tag/signature checks and website/release deployment were not executed in this toolchain-only scope.
Archive bytes match official published SHA256 over HTTPS; a detached release signature was not independently verified. Hashes do not independently establish authenticated origin.
No upstream changes, report-root edits, commits, pushes, contact or visibility changes were made by this agent.
workflow_node22_verification.raw_log_policy: Raw logs, source copies, runtime downloads and environments remain only in ignored .audit-cache/continuation/toolchain/fde. Publish portable outcomes and hashes by integrating this supplement into the existing task evidence.
